item.content:encoded:
Voters sought action on energy costs, corruption and data centers in an election environmentalists believe sets the stage for renewed climate policy.

By Marianne Lavelle, Dan Gearino

Democrats on Tuesday won control of both houses of Congress and a decisive mandate to put a check on Donald Trump’s tumultuous presidency, a victory propelled by voter anger over high prices, corruption and the unchecked spread of data centers.

item.content:encoded:
The newly launched U.S. Forest Monitor tracks satellite imagery to document forest loss over time.

By Dennis Pillion

A new satellite tracking system finds that the United States has lost 350,000 acres of forest land per year—a rate of approximately one football field every two minutes—which is the equivalent of 2.3 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions through the release of stored CO2 in the forests and lost potential carbon storage.

item.dc:creator: By Kate Waxman

I’m a Florida native and was a fellow at Inside Climate News this summer, where I covered climate and environmental justice in my home state. […]
item.content:encoded:
Voters say they want to hear more about climate. This election, candidates mostly stopped saying it.

By Kate Waxman

Hi, I’m Kate Waxman, and this is my first edition of Today’s Climate. I’m taking this newsletter over from my colleague Kiley Price, whom I admire for her sharp coverage. I’m a Florida native and was a fellow at Inside Climate News this summer, where I covered climate and environmental justice in my home state. That meant following fights over AI data centers, the homes least prepared for the super El Niño and water quality aid. Across all of that reporting, climate change kept showing up in power bills, insurance premiums and hurricane recovery, but rarely by name. That gap is what this week’s edition is about.

item.title: US Buildings Lost to Wildfires Could Triple By 2060
item.dc:creator: By Jake Bolster
item.description: The number of buildings across the contiguous United States threatened by wildfires could almost triple by 2060, according to a new study, if the country continues to ignore the perils of climate change, mismanage its forests and build homes in places where large fires naturally occur. The paper, published Tuesday in Nature Communications by researchers from […]
item.content:encoded:
The country could reduce the risk by better managing forests and housing development to account for climate change, new research suggests.

By Jake Bolster

The number of buildings across the contiguous United States threatened by wildfires could almost triple by 2060, according to a new study, if the country continues to ignore the perils of climate change, mismanage its forests and build homes in places where large fires naturally occur.

item.description: The Environmental Protection Agency late last week announced it would end a 20-plus-year effort to develop methods to monitor air pollution from factory farms, effectively shuttering the agency’s stop-and-start attempts to regulate the potentially pollutant-spewing facilities under the Clean Air Act. The announcement came just days before the midterm elections and was characterized by the […]
item.content:encoded:
The agency says it will suspend efforts, in the works for more than 20 years, to develop measures that would allow the agency to enforce bedrock clean air laws at factory farms.

By Georgina Gustin

The Environmental Protection Agency late last week announced it would end a 20-plus-year effort to develop methods to monitor air pollution from factory farms, effectively shuttering the agency’s stop-and-start attempts to regulate the potentially pollutant-spewing facilities under the Clean Air Act.

By Georgina Gustin
